arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Howe argued the Convention requires returning abducted children to their habitual residence.
Ms. Howe stated the Convention aims to prevent abduction and ensure proper court resolution.
Ms. Anders argued the ne exeat provision prevents the specific harm the Convention addresses.
Mr. Hays argued custody and access rights are distinct substantive legal concepts.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case involves a child custody dispute under the Hague Convention. The parties disagree on the legal effect of a ne exeat order. One side argues the order grants custody rights. The other side argues it only grants access rights. The Court must interpret the Convention's definitions.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of custody rights under the Hague Convention. It determines how courts handle international child removals. The outcome shapes future custody disputes involving foreign orders. It impacts the balance between parental rights and child welfare.
